skill.name: plugin-forge
skill.description: Create and maintain Claude Code plugin directories, manifests, marketplace entries, and version updates with scripted workflows and reference documentation.
skill.summary: Scaffold Claude Code plugins and keep marketplace manifests synchronized.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, or required .claude-plugin manifest paths. The scripts perform intended local file writes, and unvalidated plugin names create a path traversal risk if a crafted name is used. No prompt-injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Plugin names are used in filesystem paths without strict validation.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only kebab-case names, reject dots and path separators, resolve final paths, and require them to stay under marketplace_root/plugins.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts rewrite plugin and marketplace manifests.
remediation.suggestion: Before each write, compare the resolved target path against the expected marketplace directories and fail closed on mismatch.

remediation.issue: Documentation encourages running local scripts that modify files.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should run scripts only in trusted marketplace worktrees after reviewing the target root and plugin name.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Plugin Name Path Traversal
semantic_findings.description: The helper scripts build filesystem paths from the plugin_name argument without validating kebab-case or rejecting path separators. A crafted name can move writes outside the intended plugins directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The path components come directly from command-line plugin_name and are later used for mkdir or open writes. Exploitation requires passing a malicious name, so the confidence is high but context-dependent.

content.value_statement: Claude Code plugin setup requires exact folders, manifests, and marketplace entries. Plugin Forge provides scripts and workflows that scaffold plugins, update versions, and guide local testing.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds a new plugin directory with manifest, command, skill, and README locations.
Adds a plugin entry to an existing marketplace manifest.
Bumps semantic versions in plugin and marketplace manifests.
Explains expected plugin component paths for commands, skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers.
Provides local testing and publishing workflows for Claude Code plugins.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or later to run the included helper scripts.
Does not create finished commands, agents, hooks, or skill content.
Requires an existing marketplace manifest before script-based plugin creation.
Plugin names should be validated by the user until script safeguards are added.

use_cases.title: Create Internal Plugins
use_cases.description: Scaffold plugins for team workflows and register them in a shared marketplace.

use_cases.title: Maintain Plugin Releases
use_cases.description: Synchronize semantic versions in plugin and marketplace manifests before publishing updates.

use_cases.title: Learn Plugin Structure
use_cases.description: Review supported component locations and local testing steps before building a plugin.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code plugin named <name> in my marketplace. Use author <name> and category <category>.

prompt_templates.title: Add Plugin Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a command and skill structure to my existing plugin. Explain which files I need and where they belong.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my plugin manifest and marketplace entry, then bump the version using semantic versioning for this change: <change summary>.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Marketplace Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my plugin marketplace workflow for missing manifests, version drift, local testing gaps, and publish readiness.

output_examples.input: Create a plugin called api-helper for a local marketplace.
output: A new plugin folder is planned under the marketplace plugins directory.
The manifest and README template are created.
The marketplace entry is updated for local installation.

output_examples.input: Bump my plugin after adding a new command.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a minor version update and checks both manifest locations for the same version.

output_examples.input: Explain where hooks and MCP servers belong.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the hooks configuration path, the MCP configuration file, and the rule that components live at the plugin root.

best_practices: Use kebab-case plugin names and reject path separators before running helper scripts.
Keep plugin.json and marketplace.json versions synchronized for every release.
Test plugins locally from a trusted marketplace worktree before publishing.
anti_patterns: Running scaffolding commands in an untrusted or unclear directory.
Editing only one manifest during a release.
Putting commands, hooks, or skills inside .claude-plugin instead of the plugin root.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates plugin scaffolding, a plugin manifest, a README template, and a marketplace entry.

faq.question: Does it publish plugins automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents publishing steps, but users still control commits, pushes, and marketplace distribution.

faq.question: Can it update existing plugin versions?
faq.answer: Yes. The version helper updates plugin and marketplace manifests using major, minor, or patch changes.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex?
faq.answer: The documentation targets Claude Code plugins, but Codex can use the skill to edit files and run approved commands.

faq.question: What should I check before running scripts?
faq.answer: Confirm the marketplace root, plugin name, author details, and expected files to be modified.

faq.question: Does it generate complete plugin behavior?
faq.answer: No. It creates structure and templates. You still write the actual commands, skills, hooks, or agents.
